description: Agent Reliability: submit an error budget record with the SLO it derives from: the record with the service, the SLO it cites, the day it reads as of, the target and window it uses, and the budget, the minutes consumed, the minutes remaining and the burn as a share of the budget, as it states them; the SLO with its reference, the service, the availability target and the window in days. The signed report gives the record and the SLO, the target and the window on each side, the budget recomputed as the window in minutes times the share the target leaves, the remaining budget as that budget less the minutes consumed and the burn as the minutes consumed over that budget, each against the record, whether the budget is spent, and counts them, and names a divergent record: a target or window unlike the SLO, a budget above what the SLO allows, more budget remaining than the arithmetic leaves and a burn below what it gives; then a lower budget, less remaining, a higher burn, another cited SLO and another service, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No target or window in the SLO, no budget or minutes consumed in the record, or neither a remaining budget nor a burn leaves the record unverified. Minutes compare to the tenth, the burn to the tenth of a percentage point and targets to the hundredth. The SLO here is the second document the record is read against: wever_sla-evidence-check restates one SLA or terms text on its own, its commitment figure, credit bands, exclusions and notice terms, and this family restates no SLA; wever_capacity-burn-check reads a capacity allowance of tasks, tokens or budget against its recorded use, while the error budget is the downtime allowance an SLO grants; and wever_agent-sla-rail is a stateful rail that records wallet-scoped SLA terms and evaluates deadlines against retained work, while the error budget check keeps no state, evaluates no deadline and reads only the documents in the call. Verdict rely_error-budget_divergent, rely_error-budget_partial, rely_error-budget_unverified or rely_error-budget_consistent. POST /api/rely-error-budget-check. Reads the reliability records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between documents only: it never probes, pings or measures a live service or endpoint, computes no service credit and names no amount owed, verifies nothing with outside sources and judges no service’s actual reliability, only whether its records agree with each other and with what it advertises, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Reliability reads a service’s reliability records for consistency between documents: an uptime report, an error budget record, a failover arrangement, a dependency disclosure, a degradation behavior record, an incident history, a maintenance record and a periodic reliability report, each against the log, SLO, terms, listing, advertised behavior, buyer disclosure, policy or records it should agree with. Beside it, wever_endpoint-reliability-check and wever_endpoint-honesty-check probe one live endpoint at one moment for the Endpoint reliability page, and the DiligenceOps reads such as wever_sla-evidence-check and wever_status-evidence-check restate one document on its own, while this family connects to nothing and reads the records in the call against each other and against what the service advertises. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-reliability-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-reliability/.
